text:
lee: Hey—customer on eu-west is seeing auth failures and very high p99 for the /v1/generate endpoint, started ~09:04 UTC. Noticed requests hitting us in us-east according to the logs. anyone else?
sarah: seeing same spike in SLO graphs, p50 fine but p99 huge. traced one request and backend returned 403 from auth service.
jordan: can you paste the proxy logs? suspicious if X-Region header is getting dropped on failover.
lee: paste logs below (sanitized):
```
2026-03-17T09:03:58Z gw1 proxy: src=10.10.2.3 method=POST path=/v1/generate req_id=abc123 hdrs={Host: api.redwood.ai, X-Region: eu-west}
2026-03-17T09:03:58Z gw1 proxy: routed to backend cluster: eu-pool (instance eu-01)
2026-03-17T09:03:58Z gw1 proxy: backend eu-01 returned 500, initiating fallback
2026-03-17T09:03:58Z gw1 proxy: fallback to cluster: global-pool (instance us-12)
2026-03-17T09:03:58Z gw1 proxy: routing to us-12 with request headers={Host: api.redwood.ai}  # X-Region missing
2026-03-17T09:03:59Z auth-service us-12: returned 403 token-region-mismatch
```
maria: oh. header dropped during cluster selection. I suspect our lb healthcheck path strip or envoy route config for the failover cluster doesn't use `preserve_external_request_headers`.
sarah: i can repro locally with a small script that simulates a backend 500 then fails over. sample curl: 
```
curl -v -H "X-Region: eu-west" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -X POST https://gw-staging.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```
then force backend to 500. if header disappears on failover -> auth 403.
jordan: quick workaround: add config to copy X-Region into x-redwood-region on internal requests before failover, then auth will check both. but need root cause fix.
lee: customer impact: some EU customers seeing increased billing anomalies because requests are charged at us prices when routed to us cluster during fallback. also auth errors cause retries and extra tokens.
maria: probably regression from last envoy bump 1.26 -> 1.27 where we changed route-level header handling for virtual clusters. i'll run a bisect.
sarah: created quick dashboard: eu-west failover count and X-Region-missing ratio. posting link: https://console.redwood.ai/d/abcd/failover-debug :eyes:
deploy-bot: Deploy 2026.03.16-23:40 rolled to gw-stable (sha: a1b2c3).
jordan: can someone collect a pcap of the internal connection between gw1 and us-12 when this happens? need to confirm if header is stripped at gw or dropped by downstream.
lee: attaching repro steps and sample logs to the ticket #SUP-4829. steps: 1) send authorized request with X-Region eu-west 2) induce backend 500 (kill worker) 3) observe fallback request headers 4) confirm auth 403 and billing region tag us-east.
maria: i'll open an urgent PR to set `preserve_external_request_headers: true` on fallback clusters and include a unit test. will also add a canary to only enable for eu routes.
sarah: temporaryMitigation: suggest support patching customer project's region-affinity header to `x-region-prefer: eu` which our routing honors before failover. communicating to customer now. :thumbsup:
lee: thanks team — please ping once canary is running. i'll escalate billing/reconciliation for affected customers.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for gw-config-pr-472 on gw-canary (10% traffic).
maria: canary shows 0 auth 403s for the last 10m on eu route. rolling to 50%.
jordan: follow-up: after rollout we'll add an integration test that simulates backend failures and asserts X-Region preserved in fallback. low risk but high impact.
sarah: closing loop with customer in 30m. thx everyone. :sparkles:
